name: profile_reuse_tree_vs_dag
invariant: DAG reuse differs from tree-unfolded reconstruction (COMPLEXITY.md section 10, Counterexample 2 / section 9). Building component u once (from a, b) and binding it into three downstream assemblies gives a strictly positive reuse gain G_reuse(H) = A_tree(H) - A_DAG(H) > 0, since the tree-unfolded cost duplicates u's whole ancestor lineage (a, b, u) once per downstream consumer while the DAG cost pays for a, b, u once plus three cheap reuse edges.
explanation: history_shared reuses u=3 across v1,v2,v3 via three separate bind edges out of u. history_no_reuse independently reconstructs a fresh copy of the a-b-u lineage for every one of its three sinks, so it has no shared ancestors at all; its own reuse gain is expected to be non-positive (small and <= 0, reflecting 'no reuse occurred, and binding still cost something'), not positive -- this is an intentional contrast, not an error, per profile.py's documented caveat that G_reuse is not asserted non-negative in general, only when actual sharing exists.
